item.title: Annotate Command (annotate)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: annotate

Use annotate to add, change, or remove annotations after the backup command creates a backup.

Command Options

Backup Annotation Option (--annotation)

Annotate backup with user-defined key/value pairs.

Attach informative key/value pairs to the backup. Repeat this option to attach multiple annotations.

When --set specifies a backup, the info command includes its annotations in text output. JSON output always includes annotations.

item.title: News
item.description:
Source: https://pgbackrest.org/news.html

pgBackRest 2.59.2 Released

September 27, 2026

The pgBackRest community released pgBackRest 2.59.2. This backup and restore solution supports PostgreSQL databases and workloads of all sizes.

pgBackRest provides these backup and recovery features: parallel backup and restore; full, differential, incremental, and block incremental backups; and multiple repositories. It also supports delta restore, parallel asynchronous archiving, malware/ransomware protection, per-file checksums, and validation of enabled page checksums during backup. Other features include multiple compression types, encryption, partial/failed backup resume, standby backups, tablespaces, and links. Storage options include S3, Azure, GCS, and SFTP. pgBackRest also supports backup expiration, local or remote operation through SSH or TLS, and flexible configuration.

item.title: Archive Get Command (archive-get)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: archive-get

PostgreSQL uses this command to restore a backup or perform PITR. It can also use the command instead of streaming to keep a replica current. PostgreSQL needs WAL segments for recovery and replica maintenance.

With multiple repositories, pgBackRest searches for WAL in priority order, such as repo1, then repo2. Usually, give faster or cheaper storage higher priority. If --repo specifies a repository, pgBackRest searches only that repository.

item.title: User Guide (Debian/Ubuntu)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest 2.59.2 user guide.

Introduction

Follow this guide in order the first time. Each section depends on earlier sections. For example, Restore requires the configuration from Quick Start. After pgBackRest is running, you can use sections independently.

These examples use Debian/Ubuntu and PostgreSQL 17. You can adapt them to other Unix distributions and PostgreSQL versions. Only commands to create, start, stop, and drop clusters depend on the OS. pgBackRest commands are the same across Unix systems, although the executable location can differ. PostgreSQL versions can differ in paths, file names, and settings; some examples show these differences.

item.title: Archive Push Command (archive-push)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: archive-push

This command accepts a WAL segment from PostgreSQL. It archives the segment in each repository defined by an indexed repo-path option. See Repository for configuration details. The archive-async value determines whether pgBackRest immediately archives the segment or stores it locally first. With multiple repositories, archive-push attempts to write to as many as possible.

Configure PostgreSQL to call archive-push. See the example in Configure Archiving.

Command Options

Asynchronous Archiving Option (--archive-async)

Push/get WAL segments asynchronously.

item.title: User Guide (RHEL)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest 2.59.2 user guide.

Introduction

Follow this guide in order the first time. Each section depends on earlier sections. For example, Restore requires the configuration from Quick Start. After pgBackRest is running, you can use sections independently.

These examples use RHEL and PostgreSQL 14. You can adapt them to other Unix distributions and PostgreSQL versions. Only commands to create, start, stop, and drop clusters depend on the OS. pgBackRest commands are the same across Unix systems, although the executable location can differ. PostgreSQL versions can differ in paths, file names, and settings; some examples show these differences.

item.title: Backup Command (backup)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: backup

With multiple repositories, pgBackRest backs up to the highest priority repository, such as repo1. Use --repo to select another repository.

pgBackRest has no built-in scheduler. Use cron or another scheduler to run it.

See Perform a Backup for more details and examples.

Command Options

Backup Annotation Option (--annotation)

Annotate backup with user-defined key/value pairs.

Attach informative key/value pairs to the backup. Repeat this option to attach multiple annotations.

item.title: Command Reference
item.description:
Source: https://pgbackrest.org/command.html

Introduction

Commands execute pgBackRest functions. Each command page lists every applicable option, including options shared with other commands. The lists also include options that you can set in pgbackrest.conf.

Use the reset- prefix on the command line to reset a non-boolean option from pgbackrest.conf to its default. For example, use this feature to restore a backup directly on a repository host. Normally, pgBackRest detects the remote database host and reports an error because remote restores are not supported. Add --reset-pg1-host to ignore the remote database host and restore locally. You might also need --pg1-path to select a path other than the database host path.

item.title: Check Command (check)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: check

The check command validates pgBackRest and archive_command configuration for the specified stanza. It checks backup and archive settings for all repositories and databases configured on the current host. It detects configuration errors, especially archive errors that leave backups incomplete because required WAL segments never reached the archive. Run it on the PostgreSQL or repository host. You can also run it on a standby, but then it checks only repository configuration. A standby cannot execute pg_switch_xlog()/pg_switch_wal().

item.title: Configuration Reference
item.description:
Introduction

You can configure pgBackRest entirely with command-line parameters. For complex installations or many options, a configuration file is more practical. Its default location is /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf. If that file is absent, pgBackRest checks the old default, /etc/pgbackrest.conf.

The following option types are used:

String: A text string, commonly an identifier, password, etc.

Command line example: --stanza=demo
Configuration file example: repo1-cipher-pass=zWaf6XtpjIVZC5444yXB...

Path: Identify a location in a directory structure. Paths must start with /. They cannot contain double // and should not end with /.

item.title: Expire Command (expire)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: expire

pgBackRest rotates full backups according to a count or time period. Count-based retention keeps a specified number of backups, regardless of their creation times. Differential retention uses a count, but a differential always expires with its parent full backup. Incremental backups have no independent expiration policy. They expire with their parent full or differential backup. See Full Backup Retention and Differential Backup Retention for details and examples.

By default, pgBackRest keeps archived WAL for unexpired backups. You can change this per repository with retention-archive options, but this is not recommended. See Archive Retention for details and examples.

item.title: Release Notes
item.description:
Introduction

pgBackRest release numbers have major and minor parts. A major release may break compatibility with the previous major release. However, v2 releases fully support v1 repositories and accept all v1 options. Minor releases can add features and bug fixes. They do not change the repository format and aim to preserve option names and behavior. See the v1 documentation.

A release can include “Additional Notes”. These cover only documentation or test-suite changes and do not directly affect the pgBackRest codebase.

item.title: Frequently Asked Questions
item.description:
Introduction

These answers cover specific questions that the User Guide and references might not cover. If your issue is absent, check the pgBackRest Issues List in GitHub.

What if I get the “could not find WAL segment” error?

This error has several possible causes:

  • misconfigured archive_command
  • misconfigured pgBackRest configuration files
  • network or permissions issue
  • third party product (e.g. S3, Swift or Minio) configuration issue
  • large amount of WAL queueing to be archived

Check these items:

item.title: Help Command (help)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: help

Help has three levels. With no command, pgBackRest shows general help. With a command, such as pgbackrest help backup, it shows the command description and valid options. Add an option, such as pgbackrest help backup type, to show its full description for that command.

Command Options

Display Help Option (--help)

Display help.

Show help even without the help command. This overrides --version.

item.title: Info Command (info)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: info

The info command reports on one stanza or all stanzas. By default, text output summarizes backups for the requested stanzas. The text format can change in any release.

For machine-readable output, use --output=json. JSON includes much more information than text output. Its format stays stable unless a bug requires a change.

Use --detail-level=progress to show only progress and reduce execution time. This skips all checks except stanza availability.

item.title: Project Metrics
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest project metrics, captured for the 2.59.2 documentation snapshot.

Code Coverage

pgBackRest aims to have complete function/branch/line coverage for the core C code in /src.

Function/line coverage is complete with no exceptions.

Branch coverage excludes branches inside macros and assert() calls. Macros have separate unit tests, so each occurrence does not need testing. Asserts test conditions that should always be true and do not require complete branch coverage.

item.title: Repository Get Command (repo-get)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: repo-get

This command works like Unix cat on any supported repository type. Supply a fully qualified file name. It mainly supports administration, investigation, and testing. A normal pgBackRest setup does not require it.

For an encrypted repository, repo-get decrypts the file automatically. It does not decompress files. Pipe the output through the appropriate decompression command, such as gzip -d.

With multiple repositories, this command uses the highest priority repository, such as repo1. Use --repo to select another repository.

item.title: Repository List Command (repo-ls)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: repo-ls

This command works like Unix ls on any supported repository type. Supply an absolute path or a path relative to --repo-path. It mainly supports administration, investigation, and testing. A normal pgBackRest setup does not require it.

Default text output prints one file name per line. Use --output=json for JSON output.

With multiple repositories, this command uses the highest priority repository, such as repo1. Use --repo to select another repository.

item.title: Restore Command (restore)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: restore

By default, restore selects the latest backup from the first repository that has backups. See Quick Start - Restore a Backup. The repository order comes from pgbackrest.conf; for example, repo1 precedes repo2. Use --repo, such as --repo=1, to select a repository. Use --set to select a backup other than the latest.

For PITR with --type=time or --type=lsn, specify the target time or LSN with --target. Without --set, pgBackRest searches configured repositories in order for a backup containing the requested time or LSN. If none matches, --type=time uses the latest backup in the first repository that has backups. For --type=lsn, it selects no backup. For other PITR types, such as xid, use --set if the target precedes the latest backup. See Point-in-Time Recovery for details and examples.

item.title: Server Command (server)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: server

The pgBackRest server allows access to remote hosts without using the SSH protocol.

Command Options

TLS Server Address Option (--tls-server-address)

TLS server address.

Set the IP address on which the server accepts client requests.

default: localhost
example: --tls-server-address=*

TLS Server Authorized Clients Option (--tls-server-auth)

TLS server authorized clients.

item.title: Server Ping Command (server-ping)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: server-ping

Ping a pgBackRest TLS server to check whether it accepts connections. This checks availability only; it does not attempt authentication.

If the command line does not specify a host, use tls-server-host.

Command Options

TLS Server Address Option (--tls-server-address)

TLS server address.

Set the IP address on which the server accepts client requests.

default: localhost
example: --tls-server-address=*

TLS Server Port Option (--tls-server-port)

TLS server port.

item.title: Stanza Create Command (stanza-create)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: stanza-create

After configuring a stanza in pgbackrest.conf, run stanza-create. With multiple repositories, pgBackRest creates the stanza in each one. It skips existing stanzas, so you can safely repeat stanza-create, including after adding a repository.

See Create the Stanza for more information and an example.

Command Options

Online Option (--online)

Create on an online cluster.

Specify –no-online to create the stanza without connecting to PostgreSQL.

item.title: Stanza Delete Command (stanza-delete)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: stanza-delete

The stanza-delete command removes repository data for a stanza.

WARNING:

Use this command with care. It permanently removes every backup and archive for the specified stanza from the pgBackRest repository.

To delete a stanza:

  • Shut down the PostgreSQL cluster associated with the stanza (or use –force to override).
  • Run the stop command on the host where the stanza-delete command will be run.
  • Run the stanza-delete command.

After the command succeeds, remove the stanza from all applicable pgBackRest configuration files and environment variables.

item.title: Stanza Upgrade Command (stanza-upgrade)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: stanza-upgrade

Immediately after a PostgreSQL major version upgrade, update pg-path in all pgBackRest configurations to the new database location. Then run stanza-upgrade. It upgrades the stanza in every repository configured on the host. If the database is offline, use --no-online.

Command Options

Online Option (--online)

Update an online cluster.

Specify –no-online to upgrade the stanza without connecting to PostgreSQL.

item.title: Start Command (start)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: start

After stop prevents pgBackRest processes from running, use start to permit them again. This does not immediately start any processes. See Starting and Stopping for details and examples.

General Options

Allow Run as Root Option (--allow-root)

Allow the command to run as the root user.

By default, only restore can run as root because it manages file ownership. Other commands can create root-owned files, for example in the repository. The PostgreSQL user cannot access these files, which causes later commands to fail.

item.title: Stop Command (stop)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: stop

Prevent new pgBackRest processes from running. By default, existing processes can finish. Use --force to terminate them.

After stop completes, new pgBackRest processes return an error. See Starting and Stopping for details and examples.

Command Options

Force Option (--force)

Force all pgBackRest processes to stop.

Send TERM signals to all running pgBackRest processes for an immediate, graceful shutdown. This also stops processes started elsewhere that have remote processes on this host. For example, stop --force on the database server stops a backup that started on the backup server.

item.title: Verify Command (verify)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: verify

Verify checks whether repository backups and archives are valid.

Command Options

Output Option (--output)

Output type.

The following output types are supported:

  • none - No verify output.
  • text - Output verify information to stdout.
default: none
example: --output=text

Set Option (--set)

Backup set to verify.

item.title: Version Command (version)
item.description:
Source: pgBackRest Command Docs: version

Display the installed pgBackRest version.

Command Options

Output Option (--output)

Output type.

The following output types are supported:

  • text - Display the installed pgBackRest version as text.
  • num - Display the installed pgBackRest version as an integer.
default: text
example: --output=num

item.title: pgBackRest 2.59.2 Documentation
item.description:
Snapshot of the pgBackRest 2.59.2 documentation: https://pgbackrest.org/

Introduction

pgBackRest provides backup and restore functions for PostgreSQL. It supports large databases and workloads.

pgBackRest v2.59.2 is the current stable release. Release notes are on the Releases page.

If you like pgBackRest, give the project a star on GitHub.
